issues: wms/cmd_returns.py _create refuses any return on an order that has the same SKU on two lines, which the spec allows, because ship movements don't record their line; the unit cost and the lot/serial checks are taken over every ship of that SKU on the order rather than over the one line.

wms/cmd_serve.py Api.idempotent writes the idempotency record on a separate autocommit connection after the command's transaction has already committed, so a crash between the two leaves the change applied with no key stored, and a retry would apply it a second time.

wms/cli.py main only catches UserError, so a bad --db path, a database still locked after the 30 s timeout, or any unexpected exception crashes with a Python traceback instead of a clean error and exit code.

wms/cmd_orders.py _figures re-implements the PO received/open quantity calculation that already exists in cmd_po._lines, and the orders module also holds the available and reorder commands, which mixes responsibilities.

wms/cmd_views.py valuation --at rebuilds value by adding up movement values, while the current valuation adds up FIFO layers and rounds once, so the same moment can be valued a cent differently depending on whether --at is used.

wms/cmd_setup.py _import_products builds its multi-line stderr by joining messages with "\nerror: " inside the domain code (a CLI formatting detail leaking into it); wms/engine.py _qty repeats core.parse_qty's checks, and core.movement_json contains dead code (`unit = None`, the qty_fmt branch).
strengths: The stock engine (engine.py) is the one place for stock and cost changes: FIFO layers, consumption records for exact restores on void or transfer cancel, and average state are handled consistently, with Decimal stored as text and parameterised SQL throughout.

Each command runs in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that is rolled back on any error, including reservation expiry; on top of that, a single API lock serialises HTTP requests, so commands are all-or-nothing and stock can't be reserved twice.

The tests are behaviour-focused and broad, run on a fresh database per test, and include rule and edge-case checks, roles, rollback-on-error, idempotency replays and concurrent HTTP confirms; a weak spot is that a few tests insert rows directly with SQL, and there are two duplicate helper modules (tests/helpers.py and tests/util.py).
